rows.howToFix: Diagnose with a crankcase-vacuum test; replace the failed AOS and clean the intake tract. Inspect spark plugs, oxygen sensors and MAF for oil contamination. For track use, consider an upgraded/baffled AOS or catch-can setup. Address promptly to prevent oil-ingestion damage to cams, pistons or sensors.

Replace the failed AOS (and clean oil residue from the intake tract); tracked cars may benefit from an upgraded separator. Clear fuel-trim and misfire codes after repair and verify the smoke and idle quality are resolved.

rows.title: Cooling System Changeover/Bypass Valve and Water Pump Failure Causing Overheating

Replace the failed changeover valve(s) and/or the water pump assembly and any cracked coolant cover, then bleed/refill the system per Porsche procedure. Because the plastic impeller and pump bearings wear early, many owners pre-emptively replace the water pump around 30,000-40,000 miles and inspect hoses, the expansion tank, and radiators at the same time.

Repairs are performed at no cost under the recall.

rows.howToFix: If fuel odor, visible fuel or smoke is present, stop, switch the engine off when safe, move away and arrange towing; call emergency services for fire. Check the VIN against both 17V-054/AH01 and 19V-113/AKA3, then contact an authorized Porsche dealer to confirm open status and current remedy availability and charge. Do not buy fuel-pipe screws, a fuel rail, line or crossmember from this page; campaign status, exact condition, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: Manual Transmission 1st-to-2nd Gear Synchro Grind
rows.howToFix: Bleed the clutch hydraulic system to remove air and ensure full disengagement, and verify clutch pedal travel/master-cylinder operation. Use the correct Porsche manual-transmission fluid and allow the gearbox to warm before brisk shifting. If the synchro is already damaged, the transmission must be opened to replace the 2nd-gear synchro assembly; some cars have been addressed under warranty.

A confirmed rear main seal leak requires transmission removal — often combined with a clutch job on manual cars to save labor. Also check oil cooler and cam seals as secondary culprits.

rows.title: PCM Apple CarPlay / Touchscreen Freeze and Connection Dropouts
rows.howToFix: Reboot the PCM by holding the left head-unit (volume) knob until it restarts. To resolve the wired-CarPlay/Bluetooth conflict, 'forget' the Porsche Bluetooth pairing on the iPhone so wired CarPlay can take over the UI. Start the car, wait a moment, then connect an undamaged genuine Apple cable to an unlocked phone (no USB adapter). Apply any available PCM/software updates from the dealer.

rows.title: PCM Infotainment Freezing, CarPlay Dropouts, and Backup Camera Failure
rows.howToFix: Apply the latest PCM software/firmware update at the dealer, which resolves many freezing, CarPlay, and Bluetooth complaints. Try a PCM reset, remove and re-pair the phone, and use a known-good certified cable for wired CarPlay. If the screen remains dead or stuck in a reboot loop after software updates, the PCM display unit may need replacement.

rows.title: PDK Mechatronic Unit Valve Body Issues

Replace the rear main seal during a clutch or transmission-removal service to save labor, and renew valve-cover gaskets and spark-plug-tube seals with high-quality parts when oil is found on the plugs/coils. Clean affected ignition components and inspect coils for oil damage. Address any oil found on plugs immediately to prevent misfires.

rows.title: Turbo Wastegate Rattle at Idle
rows.howToFix: Porsche released an updated wastegate actuator with tighter tolerances. Some owners report success with adjusting the wastegate arm preload. The rattle does not cause mechanical damage but can be addressed under warranty.

Confirm coolant is not being pulled into the vacuum/changeover-valve system. Use only Porsche-approved coolant and bleed the system properly after replacement to avoid air pockets and overheating.

rows.title: Gasoline Particulate Filter (GPF/OPF) Clogging and Premature Failure
rows.howToFix: Drive the car periodically at sustained highway speed/load to allow the GPF to passively regenerate; avoid repeated short trips. Use only the manufacturer-specified low-ash (C-spec) engine oil. If limp mode or a GPF fault appears, scan for codes and have the filter/differential-pressure sensor inspected; a clogged filter may require forced regeneration or replacement. Pursue a goodwill/warranty claim for premature (low-mileage) failures.

rows.title: Gasoline Particulate Filter (OPF/GPF) Clogging and Failure
rows.howToFix: Have a dealer or Porsche specialist read the differential-pressure data and confirm whether the filter is genuinely saturated or the sensor is misreading before authorizing replacement. Force an active/service regeneration and apply the latest engine-control and GPF software updates, which have resolved many cases. Avoid repeated short, low-temperature trips and use quality fuel to promote passive regeneration. If the filter is genuinely failed, the combined GPF/catalytic-converter unit must be replaced; open a case with Porsche Customer Care to pursue goodwill coverage given the documented software involvement.

Pressure-test the system afterward and inspect the changeover valve.

rows.title: Chronic oil leaks from cooler lines, thermostat seal and chain housings
rows.howToFix: During restoration, reseal the whole oil system as a system rather than chasing one drip: replace the crimped front-cooler rubber hoses with new (ideally braided/AN-style) lines, renew the thermostat O-ring, and properly re-gasket the chain housing covers and cam towers with correct gaskets and sealant. Many restorers upgrade to a larger front cooler and braided cooler lines while everything is apart, improving both sealing and cooling margin. Doing all the seals at once — and torquing covers to spec — is the proven way to end the chronic seep for good.

rows.title: Structural rust in kidney bowls, longitudinals, floor pan and battery box
rows.howToFix: Cut out the rot and weld in correct repair panels — Porsche/OEM-pattern kidney bowls, longitudinal/inner-sill sections, floor and suspension pans and battery box are all reproduced (Stoddard, Heritage, Restoration Design). The bulletproofing step that beats the factory: after metal repair, fully seam-seal and then inject cavity wax (Wurth/Dinitrol) into every box section the factory left bare on pre-'76 cars, and re-apply a flexible underbody coating. Replicating the post-1976 hot-dip galvanizing logic with modern cavity wax is what stops the rust from ever coming back. Address blocked battery-box and sunroof/windshield drains so water can't pool again.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Timing chain tensioner collapse on pre-1984 cars destroys the engine
rows.howToFix: Retrofit the 1984-89 Carrera 3.2 pressure-fed (oil-fed) chain tensioners. These are continuously lubricated and damped by engine oil pressure instead of a self-contained spring/oil cartridge, so they cannot dry out and collapse. The bolt-on kit includes both housing covers, two external oil feed lines tapped off the oil galleries, the two Carrera tensioners and fittings (~$700-1,000 in parts). It is the universally recommended bulletproofing upgrade for any pre-'84 911. A cheaper interim fix some owners use is a bronze-bushing internal stop that prevents full collapse, but the Carrera oil-fed conversion is the proper permanent cure.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: 915 gearbox worn 2nd-gear synchros and rounded dog teeth
rows.howToFix: Rebuild the 915 with new/updated synchro rings and replace the worn 2nd-gear (and often 1st) gear sets with good dog teeth, set the correct shift-rod and shifter adjustment, and fill with a quality GL-4/GL-5 gear oil (many specialists add Swepco or a friction modifier that noticeably improves synchro feel). Restorers commonly fit updated late-style synchro components and a short-shift kit, and rebush the worn shift linkage and coupler. A properly rebuilt and correctly adjusted 915 with fresh synchros shifts cleanly — the bulletproofing is doing the rebuild right plus disciplined, non-speed-shifting driving.

rows.title: CIS airbox blows apart from an intake backfire
rows.howToFix: Install a backfire pop-off (pressure-relief) valve in the airbox — a spring-loaded flapper that vents backfire pressure harmlessly into the intake instead of letting it split the box. It's a cheap, well-documented modification (hole-saw the box, epoxy in the valve). The more durable bulletproofing route is to replace the plastic box altogether with an aftermarket aluminum CIS airbox, which simply cannot be blown apart, while still running a pop-off valve. Also fix the root cause (set CIS mixture/timing correctly and cure any lean stumble) so backfires stop happening in the first place.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Intermediate Shaft (IMS) Bearing Failure

rows.title: Rear Main Seal (RMS) Oil Leak

Some owners opt for a used or rebuilt engine. Prevention: always warm the engine fully before spirited driving and avoid short trips.

rows.title: Ignition Switch Failure / No-Start (Key Not Responding)
rows.howToFix: Replace the electrical portion of the ignition switch (a relatively inexpensive, straightforward part behind the lock barrel) — this usually cures the no-start immediately. In persistent cases the lock cylinder is replaced as well.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Intermediate Shaft (IMS) Bearing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the IMS bearing with a ceramic hybrid upgrade during clutch service. The Cayman mid-engine layout provides the same access as the Boxster for this repair.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Rear Main Seal (RMS) Oil Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the rear main seal (engine/transmission must be separated). Because the gearbox is already removed, owners and shops strongly recommend replacing the clutch at the same time, and many also replace the IMS bearing and check the AOS while the drivetrain is apart to consolidate labor.

rows.title: PDK Dual-Clutch Mechatronic / Clutch-Pack Faults
rows.howToFix: Diagnose with a Porsche scan tool. Service the PDK fluid and filter on schedule. Repair or rebuild the mechatronic unit (valve body / sensors / solenoids) — now repairable for a fraction of full transmission replacement — and replace worn clutch packs as needed.

rows.howToFix: Document consumption with a Porsche oil-consumption test. Replace a failed air-oil separator / PCV diaphragm. Severely affected engines were replaced under warranty by Porsche; otherwise monitor level closely and top up with the correct specification oil between services.

rows.title: 718 Cayman (982) Gasoline Particulate Filter (GPF/OPF) Failure
rows.howToFix: Confirm the fault via diagnostics. Apply the updated GPF/OPF software where available and fit the revised filter (e.g. part 982 254 400 AF designed to resist the problem). Use the correct low-ash specification oil and avoid only short trips. Failed units require GPF/cat assembly replacement.

rows.title: Diesel 3.0 V6 TDI EGR/DPF Clogging and AdBlue Line Splitting (EU-spec)
rows.howToFix: Force/complete a DPF regeneration with a sustained ~20-minute high-rpm drive; clean or replace the EGR valve; replace cracked AdBlue lines/connectors and top up DEF. Severe DPF clogging requires forced regen, off-car DPF cleaning, or DPF replacement. Address EGR fault codes promptly so regen can complete. Avoid chronic short-trip use.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Adaptive Air Suspension (PASM) Strut and Compressor Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the failed air spring/strut (and often the compressor and distribution/valve block). Dealer repairs commonly run $3,800 for a compressor up to $5,000-$7,000 for struts; air spring ~$1,500/side, PASM strut ~$1,300/side plus ~$1,000 labor. Aftermarket air spring kits and DIY replacement substantially reduce cost; some owners convert to conventional coil-over PASM dampers.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Fuel Pump Flange Crack and Fuel Leak (Recall ALA2 / NHTSA 20V077000)
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for open campaign ALA2 and arrange the free Porsche recall remedy. The dealer removes and reworks or replaces the service cover, inspects the filter-flange supply port, replaces a cracked flange and applies the specified protective film when required. If fuel odor or wetness is present, avoid ignition sources and have the vehicle inspected rather than attempting a retail-parts repair. Do not buy a fuel pump, flange, cover or film from this page; campaign status and the authorized VIN-specific remedy control the repair.

rows.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Clogging and Cabin Water Leaks
rows.howToFix: Confirm panoramic-roof equipment, inspect the luggage compartment and rear electronics for water, and test left and right drainage with the measured-water procedure. A trained technician should clean the rear hoses using the specified VAS 6620 tool from the underbody side and replace damaged hoses or the rear sleeve set when required; the bulletin warns that improper insertion can damage the drain. Dry affected trim and inspect electrical connections after the leak path is corrected. Do not buy generic tubing, compressed-air tools or drain sleeves from this page; the blocked location, damage and current part/VIN applicability must be verified first.

rows.title: PCM 3.1 Infotainment Failure, Reboot Loop and 2020 Update Damage
rows.howToFix: For HDD-related boot loops, the PCM unit is repaired or replaced (or the storage replaced) — dealer replacement runs roughly $2,000-$3,000. For units damaged by the 2020 update, affected owners were eligible for settlement reimbursement (up to $7,500 for documented repairs/battery replacements). Keeping software current and avoiding the faulty update mitigates the reboot cycle.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: PDK Low-Speed Shudder and Rough Engagement
rows.howToFix: PDK clutch adaptation reset via PIWIS diagnostic tool can improve symptoms temporarily. A PDK fluid change and clutch calibration helps in many cases. If shudder is severe, clutch pack replacement may be necessary.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: PDK clutch adaptation reset via PIWIS diagnostic tool can improve symptoms temporarily.

rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Premature Rear Brake Pad/Rotor Wear and Persistent Brake Squeal
rows.howToFix: Replace rear pads (and rotors when worn or grooved) at their shorter interval; on PTV cars budget for more frequent rear service. For squeal, fit Porsche-spec pads, apply caliper anti-squeal/lubricant on the abutment hardware, and properly bed-in new pads; note that some PSCB/PCCB squeal is inherent and not a defect.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace timing chain tensioners with updated parts. On the V6 engines, this requires significant front-end disassembly. Replace chains and guides at the same time if mileage exceeds 80,000 miles.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Transfer Case Seal Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace transfer case seals and top off with Porsche-specified fluid. If bearing noise is present, a full transfer case rebuild may be needed. Check transfer case fluid level and condition at every oil change.

rows.title: Turbo Coolant Line Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace turbo coolant lines with updated parts or silicone upgrades. Inspect lines carefully at every service. Consider preventive replacement at 60,000 miles on turbo models.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect lines carefully at every service.

rows.title: V6 Coolant Transfer/Vent Pipe Leak Under the Intake Manifold
rows.howToFix: Replace the cracked coolant transfer/vent pipe (parts are cheap, often under $200) — but the intake manifold, fuel lines and many connectors must be removed for access, making it a 6-8 hour job; total repair commonly $1,500-$3,500+. Always fit a new pipe, never a used plastic one, since used parts fail again from age/heat. Inspect/replace the integrated thermostat housing while in there.

rows.title: Water Pump Failure and Coolant Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the water pump with an updated OEM unit. Replace the thermostat and coolant hoses at the same time as preventive maintenance. Flush the cooling system with fresh Porsche G13 coolant.

rows.title: Air Suspension Strut and Compressor Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace failed air struts and compressor. Inspect all four struts when replacing one — they typically age at similar rates. Arnott and Bilstein offer quality aftermarket options.

rows.title: Parasitic Battery Drain
rows.howToFix: Perform a parasitic draw test to identify the offending module. Common culprits include the PCM head unit, telephone module, and comfort access system. Install a battery maintainer for vehicles that sit for extended periods. Replace the battery if it has been deeply discharged multiple times.

rows.title: Coolant Pipe and Distribution Housing Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace all plastic coolant pipes with updated or aftermarket aluminum versions. This is a labor-intensive repair on the V8 requiring intake manifold removal. Replace water pump gaskets and thermostat housing seals while the system is apart.

rows.title: PCM Infotainment System Freezing and Failure
rows.howToFix: Perform a PCM software update to the latest version. If the hardware has failed, replace the PCM head unit. Aftermarket CarPlay/Android Auto retrofit units from BimmerTech or Rennline can replace the aging OEM system.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: PDK Dual-Clutch Transmission Mechatronic Failure
rows.howToFix: PDK mechatronic unit replacement or rebuild. Maintain strict fluid change intervals at 40,000 miles. A full PDK service including clutch pack inspection is recommended at 80,000 miles.

rows.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace timing chains, tensioners, and guides. Requires engine removal or extensive rear-of-engine access. Budget $5,000-$9,000 at an independent specialist. Do not defer once symptoms appear.

rows.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
rows.howToFix: Update to the latest Porsche software version which includes improved 12V battery management. Replace the 12V battery with an AGM unit if degraded. Install a 12V battery maintainer for extended parking. Disable unnecessary always-on features in the vehicle settings.

rows.title: Charge Port Door (Power Supply Flap) Actuator Failure / Cross-Lock Fault
rows.howToFix: Record which door, direction and warning are involved, then check both sides under TI 186/24 because the cross-lock message can identify the opposite door. Inspect position sensing, harnesses, connectors, drive and module operation. Apply WLK2 only to an eligible VIN and use its campaign procedure; use the symptom-specific Porsche path for other vehicles. Do not buy an actuator, door module, harness, sensor or charging socket from this page; the failed side, cause, campaign status, current part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: DC Fast Charging Failures and Reduced Charging Speed
rows.howToFix: Update vehicle software to the latest version. Try a different charger or charging network if one consistently fails. Pre-condition the battery (use the navigation to route to a charger) before DC fast charging to achieve maximum charging speed. Report charger-specific failures to both Porsche and the charging network.

rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for ARB0 / 24V455. If open, have a Porsche center replace the front brake hoses with the revised parts free of charge. Treat a brake-fluid-low or PSM warning as urgent: stop safely, do not continue driving with suspected leakage, and have hydraulic integrity inspected. Do not buy hoses, fluid or fittings from this page; recall status, leak location, current part number, service procedure and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for ARB6, ARB7 and related NHTSA campaigns before charging or driving advice is given. rows.title: Onboard AC Charger (22 kW Option) Failure - 'Electrical System Fault'
rows.howToFix: Under warranty (including Porsche Approved Warranty), the OBC is replaced as a warranty claim. Because 22 kW units are scarce, Porsche commonly offers a goodwill payment (~€1,700) to downgrade to the stable 11 kW charger, which dealers note rarely fails. Out of warranty, a replacement can run roughly $7,000-$10,000 depending on dealer, making the 11 kW downgrade the practical fix.

rows.title: High-Voltage Battery Range Degradation
rows.howToFix: Have the battery health checked at a Porsche dealer using PIWIS diagnostics. Minimize DC fast charging to 80% and prefer AC home charging. Avoid storing the vehicle at very high or very low states of charge. Porsche provides an 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranty covering capacity loss below 70%.

rows.title: Rearview (Backup) Camera Blackout / No Image in Reverse
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for ASB2 / 25V896 and have the assistance-system control-unit software updated free of charge when open. Until repaired, use mirrors, direct observation and a spotter where necessary, and do not rely on a missing image. Outside the campaign, record whether one or multiple cameras fail and diagnose software, camera, wiring, power and communication paths. Do not buy a camera, control unit, harness or screen from this page; recall eligibility, failed path, current part number, coding and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: Infotainment and Vehicle Software Bugs
rows.howToFix: Keep the vehicle software updated to the latest version via OTA or dealer service. Perform a hard reset of the infotainment system if freezing occurs (hold power button for 10 seconds). Report persistent bugs to Porsche for inclusion in future software patches.

rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for AMB5 / 21V486 and have the power-electronics and engine-control software reprogrammed free of charge when open. If motive power is lost, activate hazards, steer and brake to a safe location and arrange service; do not attempt to continue driving. Outside the campaign, preserve complete power-electronics, motor-control and battery fault data before diagnosis. Do not buy an inverter, drive unit, control unit or battery component from this page; recall eligibility, software status, failed path, current part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: Front Suspension Clunking and Creaking
rows.howToFix: Replace worn upper strut mounts, control arm bushings, or anti-roll bar end links. Porsche has released updated parts with improved durability. Lubricate suspension contact points with silicone-based lubricant as a temporary measure.

If the VIN is outside the campaign, record warning and ride height, test pneumatic pressure and inspect the exact strut, line, valve, sensor and wiring path before condemning hardware. Do not buy a strut, air spring, compressor, valve or sensor from this page; recall eligibility, failed corner, current part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

For vehicles outside the campaign, diagnose the OCS, cushion wiring, connectors and control system under the exact Porsche procedure. Do not buy a cushion, heating mat, OCS sensor, harness or airbag component from this page; recall eligibility, fault path, current part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
